text.title: Mixed-Methods Triangulation Core Rules
text.summary: 7 testable rules for a triangulation artefact: what makes methods genuinely independent, why claims are registered before the convergence map is filled, the four permitted resolutions when methods disagree, and how confidence is capped by the weakest leg.

rule.statement: The ≥3 entries in `methods_used` MUST differ in at least two of: sampling frame, data-collection mode, and analyst. A survey and interviews run over the same recruited panel count as ONE method. Three dashboards computed over one events table count as ONE method.

rationale.source: Denzin, The Research Act (1970) — data / investigator / methodological triangulation

rule.rationale: A shared sampling frame means a shared selection bias; when two instruments over the same biased sample agree, what has been measured is the stability of that bias, not the truth of the claim — and the agreement raises stated confidence in exactly the wrong direction.

rule.statement: Each entry in `claims` MUST be a falsifiable proposition with an explicit threshold (population, behaviour, magnitude, window) and MUST be written before any leg's results are entered into `convergence_map`. Claims added after the data is read MUST be labelled `exploratory` and cannot reach `confidence=high`.
rule.rationale: A claim phrased after the data is seen is fitted to whichever leg produced the cleanest signal; the other two legs are then read as confirming a proposition that was reverse-engineered from one of them, which is a single-method finding wearing a triangulation label.

rule.statement: Every disagreement MUST appear in `divergences` with a `reconciliation_note` selecting exactly one of four causes: (a) operationalisation — the methods measured different constructs; (b) population — different sampling frames; (c) temporal — different field windows; (d) genuine, and the claim is downgraded. Dropping the dissenting method, or averaging across methods, is forbidden.
rule.rationale: Inconsistency between methods is the informative outcome, not a defect; deleting the outlier removes precisely the observation that would have falsified the claim and leaves a manufactured consensus that reads stronger than any single leg.

rule.statement: `confidence=high` requires all legs to converge AND each leg to independently meet its own bar: qualitative — saturation stated and sample composition reported; survey — N and response rate pre-specified and reported; behavioural — full population or a documented sampling rule. One divergent leg caps at `medium`. A claim resting on one method is `low` regardless of effect size.
rule.rationale: Computing confidence as a majority vote across legs lets two under-powered instruments outvote one strong one; capping at the weakest leg makes the binding constraint visible so the next study fixes that leg rather than adding a fourth weak one.

rule.statement: Any claim about future behaviour — will pay, will switch, will adopt, will churn — MUST include a revealed-preference leg (transaction, usage log, pre-order, cancellation event). Interviews plus survey alone cap such a claim at `confidence=low` even under full convergence.

rationale.source: Stated- vs revealed-preference / hypothetical-bias literature (contingent valuation)

rule.rationale: Interviews and surveys are both stated-preference instruments and share the same systematic hypothetical bias, so they converge on the same overestimate; adding the second one raises apparent agreement without adding any information about behaviour.

rule.statement: Each `methods_used` entry MUST record N, sampling frame, recruitment channel, field window, and the verbatim question wording or the exact event/metric definition used.

rationale.source: Reporting-standards practice (AAPOR survey disclosure; COREQ for qualitative work)

rule.rationale: Without the instrument text you cannot establish that two legs measured the same construct, so the convergence map is uninterpretable — agreement and disagreement become equally unreadable, and the study cannot be repeated to settle the question.

rule.statement: Do NOT run when (a) only one genuinely independent source exists and no second is obtainable inside the decision window — run the single method and record `confidence=low` instead; (b) all candidate sources derive from one underlying dataset or one recruited panel; (c) the decision is cheap and reversible, where a single leg plus a rollback is faster than triangulating; (d) the legs cannot be fielded within one window and the underlying behaviour changes faster than that window.
rule.rationale: In each case the artefact would report three columns backed by one source, which is worse than an honest single-method finding: the format itself asserts independence that does not exist.
